mainText: This is Dose of Good for Tuesday, November 17. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Four-time para-canoe world champion found alive after 20 hours at sea. Mario Queiroz went missing while training off Praia Grande, Brazil. After a search by firefighters, the Navy and friends, he was found on a rocky island in São Vicente, conscious, just dehydrated and scraped. Second: Firefly unseen since 1983 flashes back into view in the US. Pyractomena similis hadn't been recorded in over 40 years. This spring it was spotted three times in Virginia and Delaware, identified by its amber flash. Nine 'lost' fireflies have now been found again. Third: Donation lets parents watch NICU babies around the clock. At Canberra Hospital, each of the 39 cots now has a secure live-stream camera for families, funded by a A$117,600 donation. One mother of a premature baby says it gives her extra reassurance. Fourth: Japanese city turns rice paddies into flood defences. After three floods, Osaki's farmers installed more than 5,000 small earthen dams in rice paddies to hold back rainwater. They now cover 20% of the fields and also shelter birds and other wildlife. Fifth: Heat-shield textile cools rail tracks by up to 11 °C without water. Korean researchers made a magnet-mounted fabric that blocks over 85% of solar heat on rails. In 2024 and 2025 tests, rail temperatures dropped by up to 10.9 °C, helping prevent heat buckling. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
